evidence.claim: Middleby's commercial foodservice equipment group serves cooking, warming, holding, refrigeration, freezing and beverage applications across QSRs, full-service restaurants, convenience stores, hotels and institutions, and includes beverage/coffee-related brands such as Concordia, Synesso, Marco, Taylor, Wunder-Bar and others.

Middleby states that it offers beverage equipment for bars, convenience stores, and coffee shops, and describes Concordia as a provider of super-automatic espresso machines and bean-to-cup coffee brewers.

Westrock Coffee describes itself as an integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts and ingredients solutions provider offering sourcing, supply-chain management, product development, roasting, packaging and distribution services to foodservice, restaurant, convenience, hospitality, CPG and other customers.

Westrock Coffee's product offering includes whole bean and roast-and-ground coffee, single-serve cups, foodservice iced tea, retail and foodservice hot tea, extract-based products, and an RTD bottle and can beverage platform.

IFF's investor materials list a 2025 Annual Report, and company disclosures describe IFF as a creator and manufacturer of flavors, food ingredients, biotechnology-derived ingredients and scents with Taste and Food Ingredients reporting units.

memory_update.text: Add MIDD as a high-priority upstream equipment candidate for coffee, frozen beverage, beverage dispensing, refrigeration, warming/holding, automation, and restaurant throughput infrastructure.
Add WEST as a below-USD-1B exception because its direct exposure to coffee, tea, extracts, RTD, restaurant, foodservice, convenience and hospitality channels is unusually strong for this node.
Add IFF and SXT as ingredient/formulation candidates for beverage novelty, flavor systems, extracts, colors, and regulated inputs, but require segment-level proof of beverage/foodservice exposure.
Add GPK as a packaging/materials candidate tied to foodservice cups and containers for QSR beverage and snack throughput; validate against foodservice volume and paperboard cost/capacity data.

Future passes should check water filtration, ice machines, cup/lid resin suppliers, dairy/creamers, sweeteners, cocoa, coffee futures/green coffee traders, and distributor private-label beverage programs for additional public-market mappings.

node: Coffee, beverages, snacks, and daypart innovation
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the upstream/enabling stock universe for beverage-led restaurant concepts, focusing on suppliers and chokepoints rather than restaurant operators. The strongest mappings are commercial beverage/foodservice equipment, coffee and RTD beverage co-manufacturing, flavors/extracts/colors, sweetener and ingredient systems, and foodservice cups/containers. Candidates are not buy/sell recommendations; they are research leads for evidence tracking.
